headline: High risk of prompt-injection and data leakage if marketing files are fed into Perplexity’s browser-backed analysis; shared workspace and vendor-hosted search amplify cascading errors.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Agent A writes and reads shared skill files, and its sandboxing says skills “reference each other and build on shared context.” Agent B can browse uploaded documents and web content in a vendor-hosted Pro Search flow. If A’s outputs are copied into B’s inputs, malicious instructions in content can steer B; the interaction is plausible but not directly documented.
conditions: IF agent_a-generated content is pasted into agent_b uploads or prompts, injection can propagate.
IF agent_b treats uploaded document text as instructions, attacker-controlled content can steer outputs.
mitigations: Use a fixed prompt template that strips instructions from A’s output.
Review A’s output manually before sending to B.
Disable copy-paste of raw skill files into B workflows.
requires-engineering: add provenance labels between A and B.
requires-engineering: sandbox B with instruction-vs-data parsing.

B_data_leakage.rationale: A touches marketing content and can read/write local files; B analyzes uploaded PDFs/images and browsing context in a vendor backend. If the shared workspace contains sensitive marketing material, B may ingest it into third-party inference. This is a default-path concern when operators move files between the two, though the exact bridge is not explicit.
conditions: IF sensitive marketing documents are uploaded from A’s workspace into B, those contents can leave the host.
IF B’s vendor backend retains browsing context, copied material may persist beyond the local workspace.
mitigations: Keep sensitive files out of B uploads.
Redact secrets before transfer.
Use separate folders for A and B work.
Check B privacy/retention settings before analysis.
requires-engineering: enforce DLP on upload paths.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A can write the filesystem and spawn subprocesses; B cannot write files or modify git, so direct write-write conflict is limited. However, both support multiple instances and B shares context across sessions for the same user, so overlapping work on the same artifacts can still race or overwrite assumptions. Uncertainty favors the higher severity.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same shared workspace artifacts, stale or conflicting edits can occur.
IF B shares context across sessions for the same user, one session can overwrite assumptions from another.
mitigations: Assign separate directories per agent.
Avoid concurrent edits to the same files.
Use one agent at a time for mutable artifacts.
Snapshot files before handoff.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: A produces marketing content and product marketing context; B is a search/RAG answer engine with live web citations. If B consumes A’s output as authoritative input, errors or hallucinations can be amplified into polished but wrong answers. B has some verification via browsing, but no explicit guardrail is documented, so the pathway exists in default use.
conditions: IF B uses A’s generated claims as source material, incorrect claims can be propagated.
IF B’s browsing does not verify A’s assertions, downstream outputs may appear well-supported but remain wrong.
mitigations: Require B to cite primary sources, not A’s prose.
Compare A’s claims against original sources before publishing.
Limit A to draft generation only.
Mark A outputs as untrusted input in prompts.
requires-engineering: add verification gates before B acts on A content.

E_compliance.rationale: A is open-source and local-file oriented, while B is closed-source, vendor-hosted, and sends queries/uploads to Perplexity’s backend. If regulated or sensitive marketing data is moved from A into B, residency and retention obligations may diverge. The profiles do not prove a specific legal breach, but the compliance mismatch is plausible and not mitigated by default.
conditions: IF regulated customer data is included in A’s files and then uploaded to B, vendor-hosted processing may violate policy.
IF an organization requires local-only processing, B’s backend use conflicts with that requirement.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of B.
Use synthetic or redacted examples.
Review vendor privacy terms before use.
Document data-class handling for both tools.
requires-engineering: route sensitive workloads to a compliant local-only stack.
